title: Ensure Array
prompt: A TypeScript helper accepts either one value or a list of values. Write a function that always returns an array: return the input unchanged if it is already an array, otherwise wrap the single value in an array.

explanation.beginner:
Example: ensureArray("read") produces ["read"]. Identify exactly which values mean absent under the contract, then select the fallback only for those values.

Compare “keeps arrays as arrays”: input [[1,2,3]] produces [1,2,3]. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Identify exactly which values mean absent under the contract, then select the fallback only for those values.

Tempting mistake: A truthiness check also replaces 0, false, and an empty string. Nullish absence and falsiness are different rules.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “keeps arrays as arrays”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
